plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Self-serve pay-as-you-go account, no platform fee; GPU quota may need a request.

caveats: Website blocked (403), use public Vultr plans API. Fractional GPU slices not equivalent to a full GPU. Listed plan may have no currently offered regions. API hourly vs monthly costs retained without assuming a cap policy.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

SKU check 2026-09-28 (API /v2/plans?type=all + vultr.com/pricing): Vultr sells NO single-GPU H100 VM - H100 is only the 8x HGX VM ($23.92/h in the API; website "starting at $2.300/GPU/hr") or 8x bare metal. 1x L40S ($1.671/h), 2x/4x L40S and 1x A100 80 GB PCIe ($2.397/h) exist but the API lists no deployable locations for any of them (flag stock).
Full-GPU VM rates are all-in (vCPU, RAM and local disk included) and encoded as the per-GPU price with vcpu_h = ram_gib_h = 0; disk beyond 0 GiB shows as unknown although each plan bundles 1.2-13 TB.
Billing caps: cloud GPU instances are billed up to 730 h/month, bare metal and other server types up to 672 h/month; stopped instances keep billing until destroyed.

fleet.verification: Consistent usage and positive billing history; request confirms profile, organization size and use case.
fleet.notes: Console Billing > Limits shows maximum instance count and total instance cost. Request Custom Limit Adjustment or support ticket; initial numeric caps, GPU-specific allowance and turnaround are not published in reviewed guidance.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Automatic Backups run automatically but you must take a snapshot manually.
snapshot_auto.note: Nothing is captured on stop; a stopped Cloud GPU keeps its disk and keeps billing ('an instance incurs normal charges as it would when active'). Optional scheduled Automatic Backups exist for Cloud GPU (daily/weekly etc. schedule, disk only) - scheduled, not stop-triggered.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the instance state that includes the file system and disk contents.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Cloud GPU VMs only: POST /v2/snapshots {instance_id}, vultr-cli snapshot create, console. Disk only, no memory. New instances can boot from a snapshot (snapshot_id on create; snapshots usable across regions). NOT for GPU bare metal: 'No, snapshots are not available for Bare Metal instances.' $0.05/GB-month compressed.

harness_api.note: Plain GPU IaaS VM / bare metal; no agent-harness API found in docs.

egress_allowlist.quote: No, Vultr Firewall does not filter outgoing netwok traffic from your instance.
egress_allowlist.note: Firewall groups are inbound-only. The only provider-side egress control is topology: a VPC-only instance (no public IP) whose outbound path is a NAT Gateway; NAT Gateway firewall rules filter inbound port-forwarded traffic (source subnet/port), not destinations. No per-instance outbound allow/deny list.

egress_http_rules.quote: No, Vultr Firewall does not filter outgoing netwok traffic from your instance.
egress_http_rules.note: No outbound filtering at all, so no HTTP-level egress rules.

ingress_rules.quote: Vultr Firewall groups enable the creation of firewall rules to filter incoming traffic on an instance's public network interface.
ingress_rules.note: Firewall group rules by protocol/port/source IP-CIDR (IPv4/IPv6), attached per instance via API/CLI/Terraform. Also VPC-only 'Private Instance(s) behind NAT Gateway' deployment with no public IP, exposing ports only via NAT port-forward + NAT firewall rules.

guest_firewall.note: Cloud GPU is a full KVM VM with root (bare metal: whole server); iptables/nftables work. Firewall FAQ confirms instance-level firewall and Vultr Firewall both apply.

secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting proxy or secret store for instances found in docs; secrets go in via cloud-init/user-data, startup scripts or SSH like any VPS.

volume_attach.quote: Yes, you can attach up to 16 Vultr Block Storage volumes to the same Vultr Cloud Compute instance.
volume_attach.note: Block Storage (NVMe min 1 GB, HDD min 40 GB), same-location, live attach, single-attach. Docs phrase attachment in terms of 'Cloud Compute instance'; Cloud GPU VMs use the same instances API but GPU eligibility is not stated explicitly (hence medium). Not for bare metal: 'No, Vultr Block Storage volumes do not support Vultr Bare Metal Servers.'

volume_shared.quote: Vultr File System is intended for clusters of CPU or GPU systems to share stored data between them
volume_shared.note: Vultr File System (VFS): virtiofs, read-write, 'you can attach multiple Vultr Cloud Compute instances to a single Vultr File System volume provided the instance and the volume are in the same Vultr location'; instance needs Memory Backing = Shared. Block Storage is single-attach.
